commit.message:
fix(browser): paginate trusted dev release resolution so the immutable baseline survives release-list churn

The physical self-update E2E resolves an immutable published baseline with the
exact same trust resolver the runtime uses. The resolver fetched a single
newest-first page of 30 releases and required a same-core dev candidate. After
the 30 newest releases all became 0.6.6-dev line releases, every 0.6.3-dev
baseline fell off page one, resolution returned null, and every integration
push failed at published_baseline_resolution_failed - breaking the physical
E2E, the verified dev release, and therefore the autonomous delivery loop.

Resolution now scans a bounded window of newest-first pages (30 per page, at
most 10 pages) and stops at the first page containing the newest same-family
candidate. Short or empty pages end the scan; no candidate in the window
fails closed to null exactly as before. The read-only release-list GET also
gains a bounded 403/429 retry with backoff for pooled runner-IP rate limits.

Invariants preserved: fail-closed on malformed newest candidate, no fallback
to older releases, draft/stable filtering, byte-exact asset digest
verification, authority_effect stays false, zero write paths.
